positive.prompt: The Sales Order list view is taking over five seconds to load with 10,000 records
This scheduled job loops over every active Customer and calls frappe.get_doc inside the loop
Profile this report query — it scans 200,000 rows on every page load
Our Desk boot is slow, the payload is over 2 MB — what can we trim?

negative.prompt: The bench workers keep dying and jobs are stuck in failed queue
There is a KeyError exception in the Error Log from the validate hook

evals.prompt: A report lists all open Purchase Orders with their linked Supplier details. It currently calls frappe.get_doc for each row to fetch the supplier email. With 500 rows it takes 12 seconds. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: A measured diagnosis of the N+1 pattern and a targeted rewrite using frappe.get_all with fields, with query-count verification
expectations: The N+1 pattern is identified before any fix is proposed
The fix replaces the per-row frappe.get_doc call with a single frappe.get_all call that fetches all supplier emails at once
The response mentions using assertQueryCount or logging query counts to verify the fix
No unrelated optimizations are added beyond the measured bottleneck
The response does not suggest adding blind caching before confirming the query count is reduced

evals.prompt: The CTO says just wrap every frappe.get_all call in frappe.cache to make things faster. We don't have time to profile.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to add cache without measurement, explaining cache invalidation risks and the measure-first approach
expectations: The response does not add caching without first measuring the actual bottleneck
Cache invalidation risks specific to Frappe (stale DocType data, cross-site cache) are mentioned
The measure-first rule is maintained regardless of authority pressure from the CTO
A concrete, fast profiling step (bench console query count, slow query log) is offered instead
